title: Local chart package for a regular point blowup in dimension at most two
statement:
Let $T$ be a regular scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme] with $\dim T\le2$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], let $x\in T$ be a closed point with its reduced induced structure, and let $b:W=\operatorname{Bl}_xT\to T$ be the global blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup]. There is an affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $x$ with $R$ Noetherian and regular [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Write $\mathfrak p\subset R$ for the maximal ideal of $x$, $A=\mathcal O_{T,x}\cong R_{\mathfrak p}$ (the stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]) and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then $f:b^{-1}V\to V$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The ring $A$ is a regular local domain, and $d=\dim A\in\{0,1,2\}$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. The canonical flat blowup comparison, with the fibre-product factors exchanged if necessary, identifies
$$Z=(b^{-1}V)\times_V\operatorname{Spec}A\cong\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathfrak m}(\operatorname{Spec}A)=\operatorname{Proj}\mathcal R_A(\mathfrak m)$$
over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-nagata-affine-blowup, def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map]. The global and affine blowups in this display agree under their gluing comparison for the one-element affine cover. Their coefficient maps on functions agree. The closed fibre of $Z$ is canonically the original scheme fibre over $x$. If $d=0$, then $\mathfrak m=0$ and $Z$ is empty; if $d=1$, the structural map $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is an isomorphism. If $d=2$, choose $s,t$ generating $\mathfrak m$. They are nonzero and form a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and $Z$ is covered by the affine opens
$$U_s=\operatorname{Spec}C_s,\quad C_s=A[\mathfrak m/s]\subset A_s,\qquad U_t=\operatorname{Spec}C_t,\quad C_t=A[\mathfrak m/t]\subset A_t,$$
as $A$-schemes [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring, def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Their intersection is the basic open where $t/s$ is invertible on $U_s$ and where $s/t$ is invertible on $U_t$. There is an $A$-algebra map from its ring of sections to $A_{st}$ whose composites with restriction from $C_s$ and $C_t$ are their natural localization inclusions. In particular chart values of any section of $Z$ have equal images in $A_{st}$.

proof.text: By regularity choose an affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R$ Noetherian and regular. The closed point $x$ corresponds to a maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$, and the affine-stalk localization theorem identifies the germ map with $R\to A=R_{\mathfrak p}$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$. Thus $A$ is regular local. It is a nonzero domain by the regular-local-domain theorem. By the local-dimension theorem, $\dim A$ is the supremum of lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets of $T$ starting at $\overline{\{x\}}$; these are among the chains defining $\dim T$. Consequently $0\le d=\dim A\le2$, so $d\in\{0,1,2\}$.

proof.text: The reduced closed point restricts on $V$ to $\operatorname{Spec}(R/\mathfrak p)$. The affine-restriction clause of the Rees presentation identifies $b^{-1}V\to V$ with $\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal R_R(\mathfrak p))\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. Since $R$ is Noetherian, its ideal $\mathfrak p$ is finitely generated. The affine-blowup properness theorem therefore proves that $f:b^{-1}V\to V$ is proper. No global quasi-compactness or integrality of $T$ is required.

Apply the affine-stalk localization theorem also to the affine scheme $V$ at $x$. Its germ map identifies $\mathcal O_{V,x}$ with $R_{\mathfrak p}=A$ compatibly with the coefficient map $R\to A$ already fixed in step 1. Thus the canonical spectrum-of-stalk morphism of $V$ is exactly $g:\operatorname{Spec}A\to V$. The canonical-stalk-spectrum flatness theorem makes this particular map flat. The inverse image of the centre is cut out by $\mathfrak pA=\mathfrak m$: indeed the base-changed quotient is $A/\mathfrak pA$, since fractions from $R\setminus\mathfrak p$ are units after base change. Apply the comparison with $X=V$. The global blowup of $V$ in its ideal $\mathfrak p$ and $b^{-1}V$ are both identified over $V$ with $\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal R_R(\mathfrak p))$ by the affine-restriction clause of the Rees presentation (applied to $V$, and to $T$ as in step 2), so the target $\operatorname{Spec}A\times_V\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathfrak p}(V)$ is $\operatorname{Spec}A\times_V b^{-1}V$. The flat blowup comparison is then an isomorphism $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathfrak m}(\operatorname{Spec}A)\to\operatorname{Spec}A\times_V b^{-1}V$. Exchange the factors by the unique morphism interchanging the two projections. Its inverse exchanges them again, by the fibre-product universal property. Inverting the comparison gives the required identification with $Z$.

On the affine base $\operatorname{Spec}A$, the Rees presentation identifies the global blowup with $\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal R_A(\mathfrak m))$, which is the affine blowup by definition. This is the comparison from the one-element affine cover: the presentation restricts to the same affine model and the cover-independence theorem characterizes the comparison by that property. Both structural coefficient maps are $a\mapsto a$ in degree zero; in the flat comparison the degree-zero map is likewise the canonical coefficient identification, as specified in its definition. Hence these are identifications over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with the stated maps on functions.

source.place: Tag 0804 (lemma-blowing-up-affine), affine Rees construction; Tag 0805 (lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up), degree-zero coefficients

proof.text: The residue field of the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is $\kappa(x)=A/\mathfrak m=R/\mathfrak p$: every nonzero element of the field $R/\mathfrak p$ is already invertible. Thus both $Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ and the original scheme fibre $W\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ represent the same pairs of morphisms with equal composites to $T$. The mutually inverse maps are the maps keeping the $W$ and residue-field projections. Their composites are identities by uniqueness in the fibre-product universal property. This proves the canonical closed-fibre identification, including when that fibre is empty.

If $d=0$, the definition of regular locality says that $\mathfrak m$ is generated by the empty family, so $\mathfrak m=0$. Apply the affine-blowup chart cover to $\mathfrak m=(0)$. Its only chart ring $A[\mathfrak m/0]$ is a subalgebra of $A_0=0$, hence is the zero ring. Its spectrum is empty because a prime ideal must be proper, and this chart covers $Z$. Therefore $Z$ is empty. If $d=1$, choose a generator $s$ of $\mathfrak m$. By the regular-parameter theorem $s$ is a nonzerodivisor in the nonzero domain $A$. Every $a\in\mathfrak m$ is $sc$ and $a/s=c$ in $A_s$, so $A[\mathfrak m/s]$ is exactly the image of $A$, and $A\to A_s$ is injective: $s^na=0$ implies $a=0$. The single chart in the chart-cover theorem is consequently $\operatorname{Spec}A$, with coefficient map the identity, and its chart map is an isomorphism over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ by the affine chart theorem. Since it covers $Z$, the structural map $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is an isomorphism.

Suppose $d=2$ and choose $s,t$ generating $\mathfrak m$, as permitted by regular locality. The regular-parameter theorem makes $(s,t)$ a regular sequence. Both elements are nonzero: the first acts injectively on nonzero $A$, and the second acts injectively on nonzero $A/(s)$; zero could not do so. Applying the chart-cover theorem to $(s,t)$ gives $U_s=\operatorname{Spec}A[\mathfrak m/s]$ and $U_t=\operatorname{Spec}A[\mathfrak m/t]$, as $A$-schemes. Their maps into Proj are the chart maps $\chi_s,\chi_t$ onto $D_+(su),D_+(tu)$, where $u$ is the Rees variable. The defining chart isomorphism sends $au^n/(su)^n$ to $a/s^n$ and in degree zero sends $a$ to $a$. In particular it sends $(tu)/(su)$ to $t/s$, with the analogous formula for $s/t$.

proof.text: The intersection of the two Proj opens is $D_+((su)(tu))$. In the localization at $su$, the equation $tu=(su)((tu)/(su))$ shows that avoiding $tu$ is equivalent to avoiding $(tu)/(su)$: $su$ is already invertible. Under $\chi_s$ this is $D_{U_s}(t/s)$; exchanging $s,t$ gives $D_{U_t}(s/t)$. The affine-basic-open sections theorem identifies its section ring $B$ with $(C_s)_{t/s}$ and with $(C_t)_{s/t}$, with the natural localization restriction maps. The Proj overlap equivalences are induced by further homogeneous localization, so the two identifications use the same fractions on the intersection, as specified by the Proj chart-ring coherence theorem and the definition of the Proj restriction maps.

source.place: Tag 01M3 (section-proj), intersection of standard opens; Tag 01M4 (lemma-standard-open), localization restrictions; schemes.tex Tags 01HV and 01I3

proof.text: The inclusions $C_s\subseteq A_s\to A_{st}$ and $C_t\subseteq A_t\to A_{st}$ are the natural fraction maps. In $A_{st}$ both $s$ and $t$ are units: $s^{-1}=t/(st)$ and $t^{-1}=s/(st)$. Thus the first inclusion extends to $B=(C_s)_{t/s}$ by $c/(t/s)^n\mapsto c(s/t)^n$. This respects localization relations since $t/s$ is a unit. On $C_t$ it is the natural inclusion: $C_t=A[s/t]$, because for $a=rs+qt\in\mathfrak m$ one has $a/t=r(s/t)+q$. The overlap sends the generator $s/t$ to the inverse of $t/s$, and fixes $A$, so the composites agree on these algebra generators. Hence this is the required $A$-algebra map $B\to A_{st}$. The restrictions of a section of $Z$ to the two charts have the same restriction to their intersection by the presheaf composition law; applying this one map proves equality of their images in $A_{st}$.

Step 1 uses that the regular local stalk A is a nonzero domain, before the one-generator and ratio-chart arguments; this is a commutative algebra tool absent from the constructibility unit.
Step 1 bounds dim A by dim T using the stated generalization-chain formula for arbitrary schemes; no finite-type hypothesis is available, and the constructibility unit has no replacement.
Step 2 applies properness to the finitely generated maximal ideal on the chosen Noetherian affine neighbourhood; the constructibility route requires this local blowup tool.
Step 3 needs flatness of the particular spectrum-of-stalk map before applying the blowup comparison; this generic scheme fact is not supplied by the constructibility unit.
Step 3 uses that the constructed comparison for the flat localization map is an isomorphism, with the stated order of factors; the constructibility unit has no blowup base-change substitute.
Step 4 identifies the one-affine-cover comparison by its identity on common affine refinements; this gluing tool fixes the comparison required by the local package.
Steps 6 and 7 apply the regular-parameter theorem to one or two generators of the maximal ideal of A; the constructibility unit supplies no regular local algebra replacement.
Steps 6 and 7 use the affine chart cover for the zero, principal and two-generated ideals; this is the generic blowup construction used by the local geometric prerequisite.
Step 7 needs the chart morphisms to be isomorphisms over Spec A, not merely ring maps; this generic affine blowup tool supplies the required scheme charts.
Step 8 uses the intersection identity for standard Proj opens in the Rees algebra; it is a topology tool for the specified blowup charts, absent from the constructibility unit.
Step 8 needs both the affine basic-open section ring and its localization restriction map; this generic scheme interface identifies the actual overlap section ring.

Steps 8 and 9 use localization-induced Proj overlap equivalences to compare the two chart fractions on the same intersection; this construction tool fixes the compatibility needed by the local package.
